item.title: Nesso-1 open-source coarse-grained cofolding for binding affinity (Valence Labs + Recursion, bioRxiv 2026-08-03) — Pairformer trunk (drops heavy-atom diffusion module, only pair-token representations updated at Cβ/Cα-Gly and ligand heavy atoms) + ESM-2 embeddings replace MSA + separate smaller Pairformer affinity module trained on Boltz-2's BindingDB/ChEMBL/PubChem/CeMM-Fragment/MIDAS curation; ~1s/prediction on H100 vs ~20s Boltz-2 (>10× faster on 300-residue targets, >20× at 1000 residues); structural benchmarks (FoldBench/PoseBusters/Runs-N'-Poses) match closed-source TerraBind at ligand-RMSD ≤ 2Å; affinity benchmarks beat Boltz-2 on OpenBind + 25 internal biochemical assays; honest caveat that OpenBind is only modestly above molecular-weight ranking for both models; selectivity examples where Nesso-1 separates identical-compound affinities across on-/off-target pairs; open code + weights at github.com/recursionpharma/nesso — precedent for extending coarse-grained cofolding to protein-protein antibody-antigen affinity. HCV nanobody-guided E2 epitope mapping (Tzarum lab, Hebrew U Jerusalem + Law lab Scripps + Steyaert VIB-VUB Brussels, bioRxiv 2026-08-03) — camelid HCAbs used as epitope-discovery probes to bypass human VH1-69 immunodominance at AR3; two llamas immunized (E2ΔTM H77 aa 384-645 including HVR1 vs E2c3 core aa 412-645 truncated); 106 clones/48 CDRH3 families, 64 purified NbHCVs, 24 cross-genotype binders; 12-Nb lead panel with KD 2-530 nM by BLI; family 13 = strongest cross-neutralizer (>50% neut across most of Salas 14-isolate ref panel at 20 and 2 μg/mL); competition ELISA + HDX-MS (98% seq coverage on E2c3) split them into 3 classes: (1) β-sandwich engaging β5 + β6-β7 loop = AR1, competes with CD81 through β5 conformational-rearrangement mechanism — validates AR1 as functional neutralization site; (2) canonical neutralization face (front layer + β5 + CD81-binding loop) matching mAb1198/mAb1382/RM11-43 human bnAb geometry — the broadly-neutralizing class; (3) back-layer β11 = AR2, low-neutralizing; structural anchors for next-gen HCV E2 immunogen design following RSV-preF playbook, plus proof-of-concept that camelid VHH libraries surface epitopes missed by V-gene-biased human antibody repertoires. PG-LLM general-purpose LLMs for protein variant ranking (Arora/Marks/Church, Harvard Med + Wyss, bioRxiv v2 2026-08-03) — 13 LLMs benchmarked on 217 ProteinGym substitution assays (WT sequence + assay description + 50 mutant sequences → ranked by fitness; no MSA, no structure); 95 published protein predictors re-scored on same candidate sets and same Spearman ρ metric; Claude Opus 5 = 0.406 (leader), GPT-5.6 Sol = 0.402 (higher on shared subset), Opus 4.8 = 0.356, Gemini 3.5 Flash = 0.343, GPT-5.5 = 0.336, Kimi K3 = 0.314; Opus 5 beats 49/95 biomolecular baselines including 41/46 sequence-only methods, approaches ESM2-650M at 0.411 but stays below leader VenusREM at 0.523; test-time compute scaling helps but tapers; unlike sequence-only predictors, LLM performance doesn't depend on MSA depth — direct relevance for antibody variable regions where deep MSAs are unavailable; contamination-controlled sub-benchmark of 59 DMS assays from 19 studies with data first public after 2026-01 reproduces the same rank ordering; leaderboard at proteingymllm.com.
item.description: Bonus Monday midday edition — three items on cofolding acceleration, camelid-nanobody epitope discovery, and general-purpose LLMs as protein variant rankers, all bioRxiv preprints posted in the last 24-36 hours. First, Shenoy/Errington/Bengio/Kapusniak/Klaeser/Pang/Radenkovic/Tossou/Bois/Wedlake/Di Giovanni (Valence Labs + Recursion; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.08.01.742196v1 posted 2026-08-03, molecular biology): "Nesso-1: Accelerating Open-Source Binding Affinity Predictions." Architecture: cofolding blueprint with Pairformer trunk operating on token-level pairwise representations (Cβ for standard amino acids, Cα for glycine, plus ligand heavy atoms) — no heavy-atom diffusion module; MSA information eliminated and replaced by pre-trained ESM-2 embeddings following TerraBind; pairwise representation z optimized via categorical cross-entropy over distance bins; separate smaller Pairformer serves as affinity module, conditioned on frozen ESM-2 embeddings, pre-trained atom encoder, and pre-trained z with masked cropping to residues within 15Å of any ligand heavy atom. Training data: PDB pre-2021-09-30 crystal structures + AFDB distillation + SAIR distilled protein-ligand subset (structure); BindingDB + ChEMBL v34 + PubChem 1.8.1 + CeMM Fragment Dataset + MIDAS Metabolite Data (affinity); same decoy generation and data-leakage constraints as Boltz-2 including removal of 90%+ protein sequence similarity to FEP+; structure-based filtering via HPL entropy > 0.7 and pIC50 ≥ 6. Recycling: full protein context on first pass, then 22Å crop from ligand. Speed: ~1s/prediction on single H100 vs ~20s for Boltz-2; on average >10× faster, exceeding 20× on ~1000-residue proteins; cuEquivariance kernels used by both models but acceleration is larger for Nesso-1. Structural benchmarks (FoldBench, PoseBusters, Runs N' Poses): Nesso-1 matches or slightly surpasses closed-source TerraBind on ligand-RMSD ≤ 2Å success rate after 15Å local alignment, and on ligand-RMSD ≤ 2Å with LDDT-PLI > 0.8 on 6Å local region — done without proprietary ligand embeddings. Affinity benchmarks: outperforms Boltz-2 on their original benchmarks (framed as in-distribution given high chemical similarity to training data — an honest methodological caveat most cofolding papers don't foreground); highest accuracy on the OpenBind benchmark; outperforms Boltz-2 on 25 internal biochemical assays with varying chemical similarity to training data. Honest limitations: on OpenBind, even Nesso-1 only modestly beats simple molecular-weight ranking (state-of-the-field limitation on true zero-shot generalization); performance limited on some internal assays with heavily out-of-distribution chemistry. Selectivity examples: Nesso-1 separates the binding affinities of identical compounds between on-targets and closely related off-targets. Antibody-engineering relevance: Nesso-1 is small-molecule focused today but the architectural paradigm (coarse-grained cofolding with ESM-2 embeddings, no diffusion, lightweight Pairformer) transfers directly to protein-protein affinity prediction; watch for open-source coarse-grained cofolding extensions to antibody-antigen complexes over the next months. Open at github.com/recursionpharma/nesso. Second, Tarabih/Weisz/Yechezkel/Pardon/Buys/Steyaert/Giang/Fraenkel/Pompach/Law/Tzarum (Hebrew University of Jerusalem Institute of Life Sciences + VIB-VUB Centre for Structural Biology Brussels + Structural Biology Brussels VUB + Scripps Research Immunology and Microbiology + Institute of Biotechnology of the Czech Academy of Sciences BIOCEV; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.08.01.742232v1 posted 2026-08-03, biochemistry): "Distinct mechanisms of antibody-mediated HCV neutralization revealed by nanobody-guided epitope mapping." Motivation: HCV bnAb response in humans dominated by VH1-69 germline antibodies converging on AR3 on the E2 neutralization face — narrow structural sampling limits vaccine-immunogen design that assumes only V-gene-biased human sampling. Approach: two llamas immunized (one with H77 E2ΔTM aa 384-645 including HVR1, one with H77 E2c3 core aa 412-645 truncated VR2/VR3 + N448/N576 glycan removal); phage-display libraries built from peripheral blood lymphocytes; 106 distinct E2-specific clones, 48 nanobody families by CDRH3 length + ≥80% sequence identity; 64 NbHCVs expressed as His-tagged pMESy4 fusions in E. coli WK6 with affinity + SEC purification; 53 from E2ΔTM library + 11 from E2c3 library; 24 cross-bound native E1E2 across genotypes on ELISA. 12-Nb lead panel measured by BLI: KD 2-530 nM against H77 E2c3, comparable or higher affinity for heterologous HK6a E2c3 in families 8 and 13. Neutralization on Salas 14-isolate reference panel (multi-genotype, multi-tier): family 13 nanobodies show >50% neutralization across most of panel at 20 μg/mL and 2 μg/mL — strongest broad neutralization; families 1 and 8 moderate breadth (3-6 isolates at 20 μg/mL); NbHCV135/139/173 weak. Competition ELISA against domain-specific IgGs (AP33/AS412, AR3A + HC1AM + HEPC3/AR3, E1/AR1) plus CD81-LEL receptor mimic. HDX-MS at 20 s peptic-digestion time point with AnPep/pepsin column and PNGase Rc deglycosylation — 98% E2c3 sequence coverage — segregates NbHCVs into three structurally distinct classes: (1) Class 1 = β-sandwich engaging β5 strand and β6-β7 loop (adjacent to CD81 binding loop) — mechanism = interference with β5 conformational rearrangement required for productive CD81 engagement (structural basis in PDB 7MWX E2-CD81 complex); mapping consistent with hcab17 site of Ogega et al — independently validates AR1 as a functional neutralization site beyond canonical neutralization face; (2) Class 2 = front layer + β5 + CD81-binding loop = canonical neutralization face and AR3; competes strongly with AR3A, HC1AM, HEPC3, and CD81-LEL; broadly-neutralizing class; HDX profile similar to human bnAbs mAb1198/mAb1382 and rhesus RM11-43 rather than to VH1-69 consensus; family 13 sits here; (3) Class 3 = back-layer β11 = AR2 region; low neutralization. Implications for AI-driven antibody + immunogen design: (i) camelid VHH libraries as epitope-discovery probes for antigenic surfaces underrepresented in human repertoires; (ii) AR1 structurally validated as functional neutralization site with defined structural footprint — concrete second target for structure-based HCV E2 immunogen design following RSV-preF/HIV-Env-preFusion playbook; (iii) family 13 offers scaffold for germline-targeting immunogen design analogous to HIV-Env approaches. Third, Arora/Chen/Du/Marks/Church (Harvard Medical School + Wyss Institute; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.07.27.741045v2 posted 2026-08-03, bioinformatics): "PG-LLM: Benchmarking General-Purpose Language Models for Protein Variant Ranking." Benchmark: 217 ProteinGym substitution assays; each task = model receives wild-type sequence + assay description + 50 mutant sequences, ranks by predicted fitness; no MSA, no structure, no protein-specific fine-tuning; Spearman ρ against measured fitness. 13 general-purpose LLMs evaluated; 95 published protein predictors re-scored on same candidate sets with same metric (critical apples-to-apples move — specialist ProteinGym numbers usually cover the full mutant space, not a 50-mutant subsample). Headline results: Claude Opus 5 = 0.406 (leader), GPT-5.6 Sol = 0.402 (higher when the two are compared only on jointly-scored assays), Claude Opus 4.8 = 0.356, Gemini 3.5 Flash = 0.343, GPT-5.5 = 0.336, Kimi K3 = 0.314; Claude Opus 5 beats 49 of 95 biomolecular comparators including 41 of 46 sequence-only methods; approaches ESM2-650M at 0.411; leading specialist model VenusREM sits at 0.523. Test-time compute scaling (longer reasoning chains) improves LLM Spearman across GPT/Claude/Gemini families but the gains taper before catching VenusREM. Alignment-depth dependency: sequence-only specialist predictors scale strongly with MSA depth; LLMs show approximately no dependence on alignment depth (directly relevant for antibody variable regions where deep MSAs are unavailable). Contamination-controlled sub-benchmark: 59 DMS assays from 19 studies whose scores first became public after January 2026 (post-LLM training-cutoff); 3 LLMs + 7 biomolecular baselines evaluated on this held-out set; same rank ordering as primary benchmark — confirms LLM performance isn't driven by memorization of ProteinGym labels. Interpretation for antibody engineering: general-purpose LLMs now competitive as tool-free MSA-free protein variant scorers on the class of proteins (antibody CDRs, orphan proteins) where sequence-only specialist methods struggle; still meaningfully below best specialist predictors (VenusREM); obvious next step = LLM + retrieval-augmented MSA/structure tool use to close the gap. Leaderboard at proteingymllm.com; code at github.com/rohitarorayyc/proteingym-llm.

item.title: TriFlow structure-conditioned sequence design (Zhou/Cong labs, U Chicago + UT Southwestern, bioRxiv v2 2026-08-01) — RoseTTAFold-style three-track evoformer (invariant point attention + triangle multiplicative updates, no biased axial attention) trained with discrete flow matching (linear interpolation between fully-masked and native sequence along continuous-time Markov chain, parallel multi-residue decoding in as few as 10 inference steps, seconds/sequence vs hours for ColabDesign); trained on PDB with ProteinMPNN splits augmented by AFDB interacting-domain pairs; higher native sequence recovery on 1,392-structure ProteinMPNN test set than ProteinMPNN/ESM-IF/PiFold; ColabDesign backbone refoldability best across 100-1000 residue lengths with widening gap at longer lengths; 500-target RFdiffusion pipeline sweep — 16,216 backbones and 129,728 designs — TriFlow beats ProteinMPNN on 143 targets vs 68 losses, beats SolubleMPNN on 200 targets vs 93 losses; 24-therapeutic-target BindCraft benchmark: TriFlow improves structure success rate for all but one target when swapped for SolubleMPNN; experimentally validated on 3 targets (PD-L1, BBF14, Cas9), got binders for 2 of 3 with KD 5.35e-7 M for PD-L1 and 5.43e-8 M for BBF14 — matches BindCraft baseline experimental success rate at small validation scale; systematic class-I cytokine specificity design — got binders for all 31 human class I cytokines except IL-7, specificity monotonically improves with inference-time-compute (largest gain from 1 to 30 sequences per target); resources at triflow.zhoulab.io; NIH DP2GM146336 + 1R35GM160468 + CPRIT RR190071 + Welch V-I-0004-20230731. Anti-PIV3 hemagglutinin-neuraminidase antibody cross-protection (Mousa lab, Florida State + University of Georgia, J Virol 2026-07-31) — two new human mAbs 5217-2 and 5217-9 identified against parainfluenza-3 HN protein; both bind recombinant HN, recognize PIV3-infected cells, and neutralize in vitro; 5217-9 targets a previously-defined neutralizing site; 5217-2 targets a newly-mapped site — cryo-EM structure of 5217-2 Fab in complex with PIV3 HN reveals epitope adjacent to the sialic-acid receptor-binding pocket; companion cryo-EM of PIV3HN-09 (previously partially protective) confirms its epitope; hamster challenge model: 5217-2 significantly reduces PIV3 lung viral titers; PIV3HN-05 (previously shown to cross-neutralize PIV1 in vitro) protects in a PIV1 hamster challenge model — cross-subtype in-vivo protection demonstrated; structural coordinates + protective-antibody set unblock structure-based immunogen design for parainfluenza (RSV-preF playbook: cryo-EM structure of neutralizing complex, then de novo scaffold design to present epitope in rigid native-like conformation). Benchmarking Deep Learning Predictions of Mutation-Induced Fold Switching (Orban/Pierce labs, IBBR + University of Maryland + NCI, bioRxiv 2026-08-02) — GA/GB fold-switching benchmark (GA is 3-helix bundle, GB is 4-strand-plus-1-helix mixed αβ fold — point mutations at 3 key positions tip equilibrium between the folds); systematic NMR-characterized dataset of mutants that individually stabilize the 3α, 4β+, mixed, or unfolded states with quantitative fold-state populations; DL and physics-based methods evaluated including AlphaFold2-based algorithms; AlphaFold2-based tools able to predict mutant effects at individual sites (some understanding of physical effects of substitutions) but performance is variable and position-dependent; comparison with experimental stability changes highlights position-dependent success and general challenges — quantitative NMR-anchored benchmark for mutation-induced conformational state prediction, sharp test case for AlphaFold-3/Boltz/Chai/ESMFold on the hard mutation-effect task; implication for antibody engineering — mutation-effect predictions from any current structure predictor should be treated as directional signals in a design loop, not ground truth, until the position-dependent failure modes are characterized on antibody CDRs.
item.description: Monday morning edition — three items on protein-sequence generative design, antibody-based parainfluenza intervention, and a hard benchmark for structure-prediction models on mutation-induced fold switching. First, Srinivasan/Yuan/Zhang/Cong/Zhou (Zhou lab, University of Chicago + Cong lab, UT Southwestern; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2025.11.30.691458v2 posted 2026-08-01, bioinformatics): "Modeling the structure-conditioned sequence landscape for large-scale protein design with TriFlow." Method: three-track evoformer-like architecture with invariant point attention and triangle multiplicative updates (drops RoseTTAFold's biased axial attention for compute/memory reasons; keeps the triangle-update mechanism that gives AlphaFold2 its long-range geometric reasoning) trained with discrete flow matching (linear interpolation between fully-masked and native sequence along continuous-time Markov chain trajectory; decodes multiple residues in parallel at each step; sequences of any length in ~10 inference steps; seconds/sequence vs hours/backbone for ColabDesign). Training data: PDB with ProteinMPNN splits through August 2021 + AFDB interacting-domain pairs + ECOD 43,622 diverse protein domains. Motivation: ProteinMPNN's message-passing GNN has local receptive field; global attention captures long-range structural dependencies; auto-regressive decoding locks in early residues and can't backtrack — parallel refinement decoding sidesteps that failure mode (third architectural challenger to auto-regressive inverse folding in as many days after EffieDes neuro-symbolic and TriFlow's own predecessor generation). Benchmarks: (a) native sequence recovery on shared 1,392-structure ProteinMPNN test set — TriFlow beats ProteinMPNN, ESM-IF, and PiFold; exact deltas in figures rather than text; (b) ColabDesign backbone refoldability across 100-1000 residue lengths — TriFlow best at all lengths with widening gap at longer lengths, as predicted by the global-attention argument; (c) large-scale RFdiffusion binder-design sweep on 500 targets — 16,216 backbones and 129,728 sequences — TriFlow beats ProteinMPNN on 143 targets vs 68 losses (2:1 win ratio) and SolubleMPNN on 200 targets vs 93 losses (2:1); (d) 24 therapeutic targets inside BindCraft pipeline — TriFlow improves structure success rate for all but one target when swapping for SolubleMPNN. Experimental validation: 3 targets tested (PD-L1, BBF14, Cas9), binders confirmed for 2 of 3 with KD 5.35e-7 M for PD-L1 and 5.43e-8 M for BBF14 — matches BindCraft baseline experimental hit rate at this small validation scale; authors explicit that this is preliminary and that scaling wet-lab is the real test. Systematic class-I cytokine specificity design: pipeline tasked with designing binders that hit on-target cytokine while avoiding off-target family members; got binders for all 31 human class I cytokines except IL-7; specificity monotonically improves with inference-time compute (largest gain from 1 to 30 sequences per target) — directly useful operating characteristic for compute-vs-specificity trade-off. Broader relevance: anti-cytokine biologics are one of the largest therapeutic categories (checkpoint inhibitors, anti-IL-6, anti-IL-13/IL-4Rα for atopic disease); off-target family-member binding is a persistent developability and safety problem; computationally optimizing specificity at design time is a genuinely useful capability. Software at triflow.zhoulab.io. Funding: NIH DP2GM146336 + 1R35GM160468-01 + CPRIT RR190071 + Welch V-I-0004-20230731. Second, McCaffrey/Esfahani/Elbehairy/McCormick/Mousa (Department of Biomedical Sciences, Florida State University College of Medicine + Cairo University Veterinary Medicine + University of Georgia Veterinary Medicine; J Virol doi:10.1128/jvi.00502-26, PMID 42536013, online-ahead-of-print 2026-07-31): "Molecular basis for protection and cross-protection by human antibodies targeting the parainfluenza virus hemagglutinin-neuraminidase protein." Two new human monoclonal antibodies (5217-2 and 5217-9) identified against PIV3 hemagglutinin-neuraminidase (HN); both bind recombinant PIV3 HN, recognize PIV3-infected cells, and neutralize in vitro; epitope mapping by biolayer interferometry — 5217-9 targets a previously-defined neutralizing site (confirms it as therapeutically actionable), 5217-2 targets a newly-mapped site. Cryo-EM structure of 5217-2 Fab:PIV3 HN complex reveals epitope adjacent to the sialic-acid receptor-binding site — proximity sufficient for steric interference with receptor engagement as a candidate mechanism. Companion cryo-EM structure of PIV3HN-09 (previously-described antibody, partially protective) confirms its epitope. Together the two structures expand PIV3 HN antigenic landscape to two experimentally-validated neutralization sites with defined structural footprints. Hamster challenge model: 5217-2 significantly reduces PIV3 lung viral titers as prophylactic (in-vivo protection). Separately, the previously-known cross-neutralizing antibody PIV3HN-05 (in-vitro cross-neutralization of PIV1 already reported) was tested in a PIV1 hamster challenge model and reduced lung viral titers — first in-vivo demonstration of PIV1 cross-protection by a PIV3-raised antibody. Implication for AI-driven antibody / immunogen design: parainfluenza is a smaller field than RSV/HIV/flu but the pipeline is now unblocked — cryo-EM coordinates of protective-antibody complexes give computational vaccine designers concrete targets to stabilize and present, following the RSV-preF playbook of Kwong-lab-style de novo scaffold design; three candidate epitopes (5217-9 classical site, 5217-2 receptor-adjacent site, PIV3HN-05 cross-protective site) with paired protection data. Third, Felbinger/Carillo/Chen/Orban/Pierce (John Orban lab + Brian Pierce lab, Institute for Bioscience and Biotechnology Research + University of Maryland + NCI; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.08.02.742283v1 posted 2026-08-02, biophysics): "Benchmarking Deep Learning Predictions of Mutation-Induced Fold Switching." Problem: AlphaFold2-family and other DL structure predictors handle wild-type sequences of natural proteins accurately, but their prediction quality for point-mutant effects and fold-switching remains poorly characterized — real-world consequence for antibody CDR engineering where mutation-level structural change matters. Benchmark: GA/GB fold-switching system from Orban lab (GA = 3-helix bundle; GB = 4-strand-plus-1-helix mixed αβ; point mutations at three key positions tip the equilibrium toward the 3α, 4β+, mixed-population, or unfolded states — genuinely severe test since the two folds differ in topology and secondary-structure composition). Systematic NMR-characterized dataset of variants at three key positions with quantitative fold-state populations measured by NMR (one of the few solution-state techniques that can resolve equilibrium populations between two folds in the same sample). Evaluation: panel of deep-learning and physics-based modeling and design algorithms; AlphaFold2-based algorithms were able to predict mutant effects at individual sites (evidence of some understanding of physical effects of residue substitutions, not just PDB memorization); performance variable and position-dependent — success at some positions, failure at others, and same pattern in comparisons with experimentally measured stability changes; general challenges for predictive algorithms across the panel. Contribution: quantitative, NMR-anchored, systematic experimental benchmark for mutation-induced fold-state prediction — the more durable contribution than any single method comparison; usable for testing AlphaFold3, Boltz, Chai, ESMFold, and diffusion-based structure predictors as they land. Implication for antibody engineering: antibody variable regions and CDRs are structurally polymorphic; the position-dependent failure mode this paper documents limits confidence in AlphaFold2-family predictions when sampling mutations in a directed-evolution loop; mutation-effect predictions should be treated as directional signals in a design loop, not ground truth, until position-dependent failure modes are characterized on antibody-relevant systems.

item.title: EffieDes neuro-symbolic inverse folding (Schiex/Barbe, TBI Toulouse + INRAE + LISM Marseille, Adv Sci 2026-07-30) — generative neuro-symbolic protein design framework separates neural fitness estimation (EffieNN predicts pairwise 20×20 amino-acid interaction scores over residue pairs <15Å apart, defining a per-backbone Potts model) from sequence sampling (symbolic solver — stochastic optimizer or exact automated-reasoning prover — finds joint-distribution MAP without auto-regressive greedy decoding); external constraints (composition rules, multi-state objectives, positional identity) applied without retraining; on Ingraham single-chain dataset native sequence recovery 33.0% vs Rosetta 17.9%, beats Structured Transformer/GVP/ProteinMPNN on same test; frames the ProteinMPNN low-temperature-sampling trick as drift from the theoretical joint (chain-rule paradigm can't backtrack once early residue locked in); experimentally validated on two hard problems — multi-state design of orthogonal hexameric protein pairs (identical fold, self-assemble only into heteromeric pairs) and de novo selective nanobody against an immune-evasive SARS-CoV-2 variant reaching nanomolar affinity from a previously unseen CDR-loop structure; first serious challenger to auto-regressive inverse-folding orthodoxy since ProteinMPNN itself. AlphaFold2 + ensemble docking + MM/GBSA rescoring for nanobody discovery (Sun/Xing/Ma, Harbin Medical U, Chem Sci 2026-07-21, PubMed-indexed 2026-08-01) — NGS-to-functional-binder pipeline that folds camelid-immunized VHH sequences with AlphaFold2, docks against ensemble antigen conformations with HDOCK, re-scores top poses with MM/GBSA binding free-energy; SAbDab benchmark under authors' sampling settings: HDOCK Top-1 pose recovery 52% (RMSD ≤2Å), ZDOCK 26%, sequence-only AlphaFold3 18% (flagged as exploratory — 10 seeds only, not a full AF3 benchmark), ClusPro 1-4%; MM/GBSA re-ranking improves top-1 accuracy further; deployed on mesothelin, PD-1, Nectin-4: ≥70% of top-ranked candidates showed strong flow-cytometry binding to antigen-overexpressing cells (paired-cell specificity control), representative candidates confirmed nanomolar KD by SPR; recovers functional nanobodies from NGS copy-number ranks well below the most abundant post-panning clones, extending accessible sequence diversity vs random monoclonal picking; single-workstation compute (RTX 4080), ~12 min ensemble docking + 6 min MM/GBSA per VHH; code at github.com/bsu233/bslab/tree/main/VHH-Screening. item.description: Sunday morning edition — three items on generative protein design, nanobody discovery, and therapeutic-antibody developability, all published in the last two days. First, Defresne/Dessaux/Buchet/Barthe/Ammar-Khodja/Azizi/Durante/Cioci/de Givry/Roussel/Garcia-Alles/Schiex/Barbe (TBI Université de Toulouse CNRS INRAE INSA ANITI + MIAT Université de Toulouse ANITI INRAE + LISM CNRS Université d'Aix-Marseille; Advanced Science DOI 10.1002/advs.76464, PMID 42531048, PMC13422582, online-ahead-of-print 2026-07-30): "A Generative Neuro-Symbolic AI for Protein Sequence Design." Problem statement: auto-regressive inverse folding (ProteinMPNN, Structured Transformer, GVP, PiFold) samples residues sequentially conditioning each on previously fixed positions; chain rule of probability says this is theoretically equivalent to joint sampling only at temperature one, but everyone runs ProteinMPNN at temperature 0.1-0.2 because low temperature yields higher AlphaFold pLDDT — and once you drop temperature you drift from the joint, and early residues get locked in without ability to backtrack when emerging global constraints reveal a suboptimal early choice. Documented failure mode analogous to LLMs on planning, path-finding, and Sudoku. Method: neural component EffieNN takes backbone B, extracts residue environments (residual MLPs + gated MLPs, six blocks per pair), predicts pairwise interaction scores E_ij(s_i, s_j | B) as 20×20 matrices for every residue pair within 15 Å; sum defines a Potts model over the full backbone. Training loss: E-PLL (extended pseudo-loglikelihood) rather than standard PLL — E-PLL handles highly unfavorable score terms which standard PLL struggles with; datasets: Ingraham single-chain (for baseline comparison), ProteinMPNN multi-chain soluble subset (for main model). Sampling: symbolic solvers over the Potts model — stochastic optimizers (LR-BCD) or exact automated-reasoning provers — find MAP sequences directly without residue-by-residue decoding; external constraints (sequence composition rules, multi-state objectives, positional-identity constraints for symmetries) plug into the solver without neural retraining. Benchmarks: masked-residue prediction 73% recovery for buried residues, 35% for surface; confusion matrix concentrated on chemically similar pairs (L/I, D/E); predicted amino-acid frequencies match natural distributions. Full redesign NSR on Ingraham single-chain: EffieDes 33.0% vs Rosetta 17.9%, beats COORDinator and TERMinator (Potts-model-based DL baselines); beats Structured Transformer/GVP/ProteinMPNN. Training with perturbed backbone coordinates decreases NSR but increases AlphaFold pLDDT of designs. Experimental validation 1: multi-state orthogonal hexameric protein platform — pairs of proteins share identical fold but self-assemble exclusively into heteromeric pairs against natural homomeric assembly favored by the backbone (auto-regressive methods must hack this with linear combinations of logits, further drifting from probabilistic guarantee); EffieDes enforces multi-state constraint natively via equality constraints. Experimental validation 2: de novo selective nanobody against immune-evasive SARS-CoV-2 variant designed from previously unseen CDR-loop structure, experimentally characterized as nanomolar-affinity binder with selectivity for the target variant. Foundations paper — first serious challenger to auto-regressive orthodoxy since ProteinMPNN with clean story for why constrained biological problems (multi-state design, functional-site constraints) benefit from symbolic optimization over neural sampling. Second, Guo/Guan/Jin/Zhang/Wu/Sun/Li/Cao/Jia/Liu/Xing/Ma/Sun (Department of Immunology + Research Center for Pharmacoinformatics, Harbin Medical University; Chemical Science DOI 10.1039/d6sc01422d, PMID 42540367, PMC13425737, online-ahead-of-print 2026-07-21, PubMed-indexed 2026-08-01): "Integrating AlphaFold2 with physics-based ensemble docking for high-efficiency nanobody discovery." Problem: camelid-immunized cDNA libraries reach 10^9-10^10 unique clones; iterative phage-display panning is biased toward highly enriched clones and loses functional binders in less-amplified sequence space. Method: (i) fold NGS-derived candidate VHH sequences with AlphaFold2 → predicted structures; (ii) ensemble docking against antigen (multiple antigen conformations, not single-structure docking) using HDOCK; (iii) MM/GBSA re-scoring on top HDOCK poses for binding free-energy ranking. Pre-deployment benchmark on SAbDab nanobody-antigen co-crystals — Top-1 pose recovery at ≤2Å RMSD: HDOCK 52%, ZDOCK 26%, sequence-only AlphaFold3 18% (10 seeds per interaction, flagged as exploratory not a full AF3 benchmark — a rigorous AF3 evaluation would need substantially expanded sampling), ClusPro 1%, ClusPro-AM 4%; HDOCK bimodal distribution (successful cases ≤2Å, failures >10Å); MM/GBSA re-scoring further improves top-1 recovery. Deployment on three antigens: mesothelin (MSLN), PD-1, Nectin-4. Antigen-overexpressing cell lines and matched vector controls (paired-cell design controls background); nanobodies expressed in E. coli Rosetta with C-terminal 6×His; flow cytometry, ELISA, SPR readouts. Results: ≥7/10 top-ranked candidates for each target showed complete or near-complete positive flow-cytometry shift on antigen-overexpressing cells at ~100 nM with no signal on vector controls; representative candidates confirmed nanomolar KD by SPR (Biacore 8K, 1:1 Langmuir). Compared against random-selection monoclonal-clone picking, workflow improves hit recovery while reducing sequence redundancy — accesses functional nanobodies from NGS copy-number ranks well below the most abundant post-panning clones. Compute: Intel Core i7-13700KF + NVIDIA RTX 4080, ~12 min ensemble docking + 6 min MM/GBSA per VHH; code at github.com/bsu233/bslab/tree/main/VHH-Screening. Deployment-ready small-lab pipeline for closing the panning-bottleneck problem in camelid nanobody discovery. Third, Paidi/Ibrahim/Stepurska/Zarzar/Izadi/Rude/Luu/Kovner/O'Connor/Bol/Mehta/Andersen/Stephens/Makowski/Heisler/Swartz/Carter/Baginski (Genentech Analytical Development + Pharmaceutical Development + Antibody Engineering, South San Francisco; MAbs DOI 10.1080/19420862.2026.2709948, PMID 42533550, online 2026-07-30): "Self-interaction nanoparticle spectroscopy predicts high-concentration viscosity of therapeutic IgG1 antibodies." Problem: subcutaneous biologics require >150 mg/mL formulations; some IgG1s become too viscous to inject through a standard needle at that concentration; viscosity driven by nonspecific self-association, hard to predict from sequence or low-concentration measurements; gold-standard direct rheometry requires milligram quantities and is low-throughput, so bad-actor candidates aren't caught until process development. Method: characterize 96 IgG1 antibodies across (i) charge-stabilized SINS (CS-SINS, gold nanoparticles stabilized by surface charge, readout self-interaction perturbation), (ii) PEG-stabilized SINS (PS-SINS, PEG-coated nanoparticles screen charge and read a more purely hydrophobic self-interaction signal), (iii) dynamic light scattering (DLS), (iv) in-silico descriptors (surface hydrophobicity, patch analysis, charge properties); train random-forest binary classifier (high vs low viscosity). Results: CS-SINS strongly correlates with computed charge — limited orthogonal information beyond in-silico charge analysis; PS-SINS provides orthogonal information — integrating PS-SINS + in-silico + DLS significantly improves random-forest accuracy over any single component; PS-SINS measured in multiple buffers captures complementary buffer-specific signals, achieves comparable accuracy without DLS (removes one instrument-time-heavy readout). Within-molecule mechanistic validation on Fc-region variants of trastuzumab and omalizumab (clinical antibodies): PS-SINS scores follow strong logarithmic relationship with high-concentration viscosity, Pearson r=0.72 (trastuzumab) and r=0.85 (omalizumab) — direct mechanistic link, not just cross-panel correlation; PS-SINS performs reliably on one-column Protein-A purified samples (material state at very early antibody engineering stages, before polishing steps) — shifts developability triage upstream, into the phase where candidates can still be discarded cheaply. Scope caveat: IgG1-only, conventional monoclonals; bispecifics and extended-CDR-H3 formats not addressed (relevant limitation given yesterday's Fab paper on CDR-H3 hydrophobic-patch predictors) — but on standard IgG1 pipelines, deployment-ready from Genentech's own Antibody Engineering group with trastuzumab and omalizumab variant validation.

item.title: Human Bindome proteome-scale binder atlas (Correia lab, EPFL, bioRxiv 2026-07-30) — 306,146 in-silico designed binder candidates covering 8,296 human proteins (40.9% of proteome, 77.8% of the "targetable" domain-level proteome); accelerated parallelized BindCraft on domain-segmented AlphaFold-DB targets, 90-residue binders, filter thresholds pLDDT>0.8 & normalized iPAE<0.35 (median 0.92 / 0.23); ~30 candidates/domain, 78% of CATH superfamilies covered but only 13.9% of proteome surface area contacted (epitope-coverage gap); binders preferentially engage evolutionarily-conserved surface (P<1e-300 vs surface control, conservation increases with binder-consensus threshold) and functional sites (26% of allosteric-annotated targets have overlapping binder, ~50% of PPI interfaces overlap, PTM/metal/nucleotide sites hit); interfaces native-like in size/polarity but helix-biased on binder side (17% novel folds, ~0.3 median interface TM-score vs PPIRef); interactive web (bindome.epfl.ch) + 3D-Beacons API + MCP-server for LLM-native natural-language querying; HuggingFace leakage-controlled splits (205,553 train / 21,205 val / 21,955 test) as a distillation corpus for next-generation binder-design models. SE(3)-MeanFlow few-step protein backbone generation (Bai/Zhang Purdue + Kolouri Vanderbilt, arXiv 2026-07-29) — extends MeanFlow from Euclidean to SE(3) Lie groups by exploiting SE(3)=SO(3)×R^3 decomposition to derive closed-form simulation-free average-velocity training targets separately in so(3) and R^3 (no parallel transport required); α-Flow warmup removes JVP from rotation branch, small-t stabilized MeanFlow loss for pretraining, rectification-based post-training on top; on SCOPe (3,673 backbones, length 60-128): 100-step designability 93.6% vs QFlow 88.5% at same budget vs FrameFlow 84.9% at 500 steps; 20-step 86.7% vs QFlow 77.8%; 10-step 72.8% vs QFlow 55.9% — 5x inference-cost reduction with modest designability loss; diversity-TM tradeoff (0.415 vs QFlow 0.393); direct antibody-engineering relevance: drop-in acceleration for antibody-backbone generators built on flow-matching baselines. Speculative decoding for genomic and proteomic foundation models (Georgakopoulos-Soares UT Austin + BSRC Fleming + MBZUAI, Bioinformatics 2026-07-31) — probabilistic speculative decoding applied to DNAGPT, ProGen2, ProtGPT2: lightweight draft model proposes token spans, target model verifies in parallel while preserving target sampling distribution exactly (lossless speedup); systematic sweep across speculation window length, temperature, draft architecture, prompt length; consistent 1.2-1.4x average tokens-per-second gains (max 2x), no change in output distribution — immediately deployable acceleration for ProGen2/ProtGPT2 antibody-adjacent sequence generation loops; code at github.com/Georgakopoulos-Soares-lab/BioSpecDec.
item.description: Bonus Saturday-evening edition — three items on the AI-for-protein stack at different levels (data resource / generative method / inference efficiency). First, Wenckstern/Díaz-Rovira/Kuhn/Ban/Correia (EPFL School of Engineering + TUM + ETH Zurich + Toronto Donnelly + AITHYRA Vienna + EMBL-EBI; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.07.30.741542v1, synthetic biology, 2026-07-30): "The Human Bindome: A Proteome-scale Atlas of Designed Binder Candidates." Method: PAE-based graph clustering (pae_to_domain, resolution 1.0, PAE cutoff 15 Å, ±2 buffer residues, gap merge ≤21 residues) segments full-length AFDB v6 human structural models into structural domains; targetable domains filtered on mean pLDDT≥0.7, length 30-550, normalized radius of gyration ≤5.0, Cα contact density ≥2.0, no membrane overlap, excluding pure single/double helix or loop-only DSSP annotations; BindCraft (backprop-through-AF + ProteinMPNN filtering) parallelized across SLURM array with two accelerations: fixed 90-residue binder length (avoids ColabFold class-instance recompilation of AF + ProteinMPNN), domain-cropped targets (superlinear runtime reduction), post-hoc superimposition onto full-length target with clash rejection against structured non-target regions (retention only where clash region has high PAE or low pLDDT). Every candidate carries: predicted binder-target complex structure, 90-residue defined sequence, in-silico confidence metrics (BindCraft-inherited: pLDDT>0.8, normalized iPAE<0.35). Coverage: 306,146 candidates against 8,296 targets (77.8% of the targetable proteome, 40.9% of the full human proteome); median pLDDT 0.92 and median iPAE 0.23 (well inside acceptance thresholds — not skewed toward filter borders); ~30 candidates per targeted domain, ~37 per target protein. Comparison to prior affinity-reagent resources: Antibodypedia 91.9% target coverage (commercial mAbs, poorly characterized sequences), ABCD 6.9% (chemically-defined), SAbDab 2.4% (PDB antibody-antigen), Biocompare 2.9%; Bindome is 2nd largest by target coverage and largest resource with openly available sequences + structural models + confidence metrics. Structural coverage: 78.2% of 1,055 CATH superfamilies represented in the target set have ≥1 designed binder; 2D UMAP of TM-score all-vs-all distances shows broad structural-space coverage with untargeted regions concentrated in integral-membrane proteins. Surface coverage: 64.5% of proteome surface targetable, only 13.9% actually contacted by ≥1 binder — per-target epitope coverage sparse, flagged as remaining methodological gap. Epitope characterization: conservation-vs-surface-control paired Wilcoxon at three consensus thresholds (any binder, ≥30%, ≥90% of binders per target); all P<1e-300 (below double-precision floor), and epitope conservation monotonically increases with binder-consensus threshold. Interface comparison to PINDER native PPIs: interface area matches native mean but narrower distribution (fixed 90-residue binder), slightly higher polar-residue fraction; secondary-structure pairing strongly enriched for helix-on-helix and helix-on-loop (BindCraft/RFdiffusion known bias), median interface TM-score against PPIRef ~0.3 (interfaces largely novel), only 17.3% of binder folds have max TM<0.5 vs AF Database (folds mostly reuse existing structural motifs). Induced fit: 4% of binders and 8% of targets show interface Cα RMSD>2 Å between bound and unbound AF prediction (target-side adaptation notable because target is templated). Functional overlap: 26% of ASD-annotated allosteric targets have binder candidate whose epitope overlaps the annotated allosteric site (examples: AKT1 PDB 6HHH, TEAD2 6E5G, DUSP10 6MC1); ~50% of PINDER homo/heteromeric interfaces overlap ≥1 binder epitope; UniProt-annotated PTM sites (phosphorylation and acetylation largest), metal-ion sites, and nucleotide/cofactor sites frequently hit; ~25% of ligand-binding sites overlap ≥1 binder epitope; 148 targets have binders overlapping DNA-binding regions. Illustrative cases: RIG-I/DDX58 phosphorylation-site binder, TP53 DNA-binding-surface binder, SOD1 dimer- and CCS-heteromer-interface binders (PDB 3ECU, 6FP6). Access: bindome.epfl.ch (interactive web UI with UniProt search + full-length-context display + confidence-metric ranking + bulk download); 3D-Beacons API (standardized programmatic retrieval, PDBe-KB integration); MCP server (LLM-native natural-language querying with iterative refinement); HuggingFace dataset wjulius/HumanBindome with interface-clustered leakage-controlled splits: 205,553 train / 21,205 val / 21,955 test complexes. Limitations: no wet-lab validation of the 306,146 candidates (BindCraft priors 10-100% success across previously tested targets); paralog cross-reactivity risk heightened by preferential engagement of conserved epitopes and family-level epitope convergence; 90-residue helix-biased binder format is not an immunoglobulin — the resource is a proteome-scale prior on designable-binder distribution, not an antibody generator, but the accompanying distillation dataset is a large training corpus for next-generation binder-design and interface-prediction models that could feed antibody-specific work downstream. Second, Bai/Lu/Liu/Akbari/Wang/He/Wang/Lin/Kolouri/Zhang (Purdue Math + Purdue ECE + Purdue Biochem + Purdue Statistics + Purdue CS + Vanderbilt CS + Freie Universität Berlin; arXiv:2607.27431v1 cs.LG, 2026-07-29): "SE(3)-MeanFlow: Few-Step Protein Backbone Generation on Lie Groups." Motivation: current SE(3)-native generative backbone models (FrameDiff, RFdiffusion, FoldFlow, FrameFlow, QFlow/ReQFlow) require 100-500 network function evaluations per sample, each involving a Lie-group exponential map — this is the wall for high-throughput screening campaigns. MeanFlow (Geng et al 2026) proposed learning the average velocity of a Euclidean flow between times s and t, yielding a simulation-free training objective and 1-NFE inference; direct extension to SE(3) is ill-posed because velocities at different points live in different tangent spaces. Riemannian MeanFlow with parallel transport (Zhong et al 2026) handles the manifold case at full generality; Riemannian MeanFlow in Lie algebra (Woo et al 2026) is a concurrent alternative. Central contribution: leverage SE(3)=SO(3)×R^3 decomposition to derive integration-based MeanFlow identity separately in Lie algebra so(3) and in R^3 — closed-form simulation-free training targets without parallel transport. Numerical stabilization: SE(3) α-Flow warmup objective removes JVP (Jacobian-vector-product) from the rotation branch, followed by small-t stabilized MeanFlow loss for the remainder of pretraining; rectification-based post-training (following ReQFlow recipe) yields Rec-SE3-MF final model. Implementation: rotation matrices under decoupled SE(3) representation (Yim et al 2023), IPA trunk with rotation-matrix input state (R_t, x_t) conditioned on two times (s,t) via shared time embedding + per-block AdaLN-Zero gate, predicts endpoints. Trained on 4×H100 GPUs on QFlow/ReQFlow codebase. Benchmark: SCOPe 3,673 backbones length 60-128; designability = fraction of 10 backbones per length whose scRMSD<2Å (self-consistency RMSD via ProteinMPNN sequence redesign + AF2 structure re-prediction); diversity and novelty TM-scores. Results (Rec-SE3-MF vs baselines): 500 steps FrameFlow 84.9% designability; 100 steps QFlow 88.5%, RMF 83.2%, Rec-SE3-MF 93.6% (best); 50 steps QFlow 87.0%, RMF 82.5%, Rec-SE3-MF 90.6%; 20 steps QFlow 77.8%, RMF 80.6%, Rec-SE3-MF 86.7%; 10 steps QFlow 55.9%, RMF 77.8%, Rec-SE3-MF 72.8% — Lie-group-native MeanFlow retains >86% designability at 20 NFE where QFlow drops below 78%; even at 10 NFE remains usable. Cost: diversity-TM 0.415 (Rec-SE3-MF, 100 steps) vs 0.393 (QFlow), 0.369 (FrameFlow) — modestly tighter mode coverage. Novelty-TM comparable across methods (~0.7). Practical implication for antibody engineering: not an antibody generator (SCOPe-trained unconditional backbone) but SE(3)-MeanFlow objective is a drop-in acceleration for any antibody-backbone generator built on FrameFlow/QFlow — 5× inference-cost reduction for antibody scaffold sampling in downstream Boltz/AF3 screening pipelines with modest designability tradeoff. Code integrated into public QFlow/ReQFlow codebase. Third, Provatas/Karatzikos/Koilakos/Patsakis/Tzanakakis/Nayak/Pavlopoulos/Mouratidis/Avgoulas/Georgakopoulos-Soares (UT Austin Dell Pediatric Research Institute + BSRC "Alexander Fleming" Greece + MBZUAI UAE; Bioinformatics DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag579, PMID 42536416, online-ahead-of-print 2026-07-31): "Accelerating inference in genomic and proteomic foundation models via speculative decoding." Problem: autoregressive genomic foundation model (GFM = DNAGPT) and protein foundation models (PFM = ProGen2, ProtGPT2) latency in long-sequence generation is dominated by per-token transformer forward-passes. Method: probabilistic variant of speculative decoding (Leviathan et al 2023) — lightweight draft model proposes short token spans; large target model verifies or corrects tokens in parallel via a single forward pass; verification step preserves the target model's exact sampling distribution (lossless at token-distribution level). Systematic sweep: speculation window length, sampling temperature, draft model architecture (multiple lightweight draft configurations tested per target), prompt length; measured tokens-per-second across configurations with multiple runs for statistical reliability. Results: consistent speedups across all three foundation models over standard KV-cached autoregressive decoding; maximum observed speedup ~2x (100% increase), average 1.2-1.4x (20-40% throughput gain); output distribution unchanged — target model predictions statistically indistinguishable pre/post speculative decoding. Code: github.com/Georgakopoulos-Soares-lab/BioSpecDec. Relevance for antibody engineering: direct drop-in for any pipeline using ProGen2 or ProtGPT2 for CDR/full-variable-region autoregressive generation; the 20-40% throughput gain is small per single-run but compounds meaningfully across mask-infilling or repeat-sampling design loops running fixed models over millions of prompts; does not extend to non-autoregressive antibody-specific models like AbLang or ESM-family encoder models. The recipe is model-agnostic: any autoregressive PLM can be accelerated by training a matched draft model — antibody-specific autoregressive LMs (IgLM, p-IgGen) can adopt the same technique with their own draft-model training runs.

item.title: aSR29-ACE2-Fc cryptic-epitope nanobody bispecific (Jin lab, USTC + Academy of Military Medical Sciences, J Virol 2026-07-30) — alternating SARS1/SARS2 RBD immunization in alpaca elicits 4 cross-reactive nanobodies with pM-nM affinity to SARS1/SARS2 RBDs and Omicron BA.1/BA.2/BA.5/XBB/BQ.1.1/XBB.1.5 spike; 2.68 Å ternary crystal (aSR29:aSR347:SARS1 RBD) shows aSR29 contacts 12 residues in a cryptic conserved epitope at the inner base of the RBD (inaccessible to conventional IgG paratopes by steric shielding); aSR29 potently neutralizes SARS1, SARS2, and Omicron subvariants including XBB.1.5 and BQ.1.1; bispecific aSR29-ACE2-Fc fusion combines cryptic-epitope recognition with ACE2-decoy attachment blockade for 33-fold neutralization boost vs parental aSR29-Fc, with mutation-resistance built in (virus can't escape ACE2 without also losing its actual receptor). Vespertilionid bat dual IgH loci (Pursell/Boyd, Stanford Pathology + Frank lab Tulane, Sci Adv 2026-07-31) — first documented mammalian dual IgH loci; A-IGH (272 kb chr5, 33 V-genes, 15% pseudogenes) and B-IGH (918 kb chr24, 99 V-genes, 46.5% pseudogenes) with full mammalian architecture on both; phylogenetic reconstruction across 34 bat species places duplication at Vespertilionidae ancestor ~26-37 Mya (convergent with salmonid fish IgH duplication but independent mechanism); 62,747-cell scRNA-seq on Eptesicus fuscus splenocytes shows: allelic exclusion intact (2% double in-frame CDR-H3 consistent with sequencing doublets); ordered rearrangement A-IGH first (naive A:B ratio 3.41 vs 2.25 expected); IgA class-switched cells favor A-IGH (38 vs 7 per animal); class-switched B-IGH cells carry lower SHM than A-IGH (suggesting reduced AID access to B-IGH in switched cells); V-gene family usage differs sharply (A-IGH VH1-enriched, B-IGH VH7/VH6-enriched). Extended-CDR-H3 human Fab developability (Svilenov lab, TUM + Ghent, J Pharm Sci 2026-07-31, abstract-only) — 5 human Fabs with long CDR-H3s run through integrated experimental + MD-simulation developability panel (secretion, homogeneity, conformational stability, colloidal stability, non-specific binding); the 5 Fabs split across the liability panel without correlation to CDR-H3 length itself; sequence composition and MD-observed loop flexibility drive the liabilities, not length; argues against length-based early-stage filters and for mechanistically-informed developability triage on extended-loop candidates.
item.description: Bonus Saturday-afternoon edition — three items from the peer-reviewed journal side (not fresh from bioRxiv 2026-07-31, which fed the morning episode). First, Zeng/Zhang/Ma/Jin (University of Science and Technology of China + Academy of Military Medical Sciences; J Virol doi:10.1128/jvi.00608-26, 2026-07-30 online-ahead-of-print): "ACE2-fused nanobody targeting a cryptic RBD epitope broadly neutralizes SARS-like viruses." Strategy: alternating alpaca immunization with SARS1 and SARS2 RBDs (3 rounds each) biases the polyclonal response toward conserved cross-reactive surface. Phage panning + phage-ELISA + SPR yielded 4 cross-binding nanobodies (aSR29, aSR196, aSR347, aSR348) with SARS1 KD 3.4e-5 to 2.82 nM and SARS2 KD 1.48 pM to 0.5 nM; all four cross-bind Omicron RBDs BA.1/BA.2/BA.5/XBB/BQ.1.1 and XBB.1.5 spike with pM-nM affinities (0.016 pM to 0.85 nM across the panel). Crystal structure of ternary aSR29:aSR347:SARS1-RBD complex at 2.68 Å (PEG6000/Tris pH 7.5, molecular replacement): aSR29 contacts 12 SARS1 RBD residues (S362-Y367, G368, G391, P399, Q401, D414, F416) at the inner base of the RBD — a cryptic conserved epitope shielded from conventional IgG paratopes by steric hindrance and accessible only to compact single-domain camelid VHH geometry. Because the epitope is conserved across SARS1/SARS2/Omicron variants, aSR29 neutralization is escape-resistant against XBB.1.5 and BQ.1.1. Engineered bispecific aSR29-ACE2-Fc: cryptic-epitope arm + ACE2 decoy arm (blocks viral attachment through the receptor-binding motif); the two arms bind independent non-overlapping regions of RBD synergistically, yielding 33-fold neutralization boost vs parental aSR29-Fc against wild-type SARS2. Strategic argument: nanobody-ACE2 decoy fusions as a mutation-resistant pandemic-preparedness template since the virus cannot escape an ACE2 decoy without also losing binding to its own receptor. Transferable engineering lessons: (i) alternating immunization against paired divergent antigens as a scalable in-vivo way to bias germinal-center response toward conserved surface without needing computational immunogen design; (ii) nanobody geometry accesses cryptic epitopes inaccessible to conventional IgG paratopes; (iii) antibody-natural-ligand fusions guarantee mutation-resistant activity via a decoy the virus cannot escape without losing its own receptor. Second, Pursell/Reers/Mikelov/Kotagiri/Lam/Ellison/Boyd/Frank (Stanford Pathology + Tulane School of Science and Engineering + Monash + CDC Poxvirus and Rabies Branch; Sci Adv doi:10.1126/sciadv.aeb6714, 2026-07-31): "Immunoglobulin heavy chain locus duplication in bats." Long-read genome assembly of Eptesicus fuscus (DD_ASM_mEF_20220401) reveals two IgH loci on separate chromosomes — A-IGH on chr5 (272 kb, 33 IGHV genes, 15% pseudogenes; enriched for VH1) and B-IGH on chr24 (918 kb, 99 IGHV genes, 46.5% pseudogenes; enriched for VH7 and VH6, only locus with functional VH6/VH7). Both loci carry canonical mammalian V/D/J/CH architecture (IGHM, IGHD, IGHG, IGHE, IGHA) with intact AID switch-motif clustering upstream of each constant gene, and flanking genes (TMEM212/CRIP1 for A-IGH, MXL for B-IGH). Between-locus IGHV UniFrac distance 0.85 (85% of V-gene evolution is locus-specific); A-IGH V genes phylogenetically clustered (MPD z=-1.84, purifying selection) while B-IGH V genes over-dispersed (MPD z=+1.46, diversifying selection). Cross-species genome analysis of 34 bat species: duplication present in every vespertilionid examined except Antrozous pallidus; IGHM sequences form two well-supported clades by locus of origin with species topology mirroring known phylogeny inside each clade → single duplication event at Vespertilionidae ancestor ~26-37 Mya, convergent with salmonid fish (independent mechanism — no whole-genome duplication in bats). scRNA-seq on 62,747 splenocytes from n=4 E. fuscus with paired BCR sequencing and 5'RACE bulk BCR from n=6 (307,312 productive rearrangements) shows: (a) allelic exclusion intact — 2.0% of 9,922 B-cells with in-frame CDR-H3 have two productive heavy-chain transcripts, consistent with expected doublet artifact; (b) ordered rearrangement with A-IGH first — naive B-cell A-IGH:B-IGH ratio 3.41 (expected 2.25 for pure sequential model, 1.0 for random) suggesting either strongly ordered rearrangement or negative selection against B-IGH-expressing naives; (c) IgA class-switching biased strongly toward A-IGH (mean 38 IgA cells from A-IGH vs 7 from B-IGH per bat); (d) class-switched B-IGH cells carry substantially lower SHM than A-IGH counterparts (P<0.001), suggesting reduced AID access/activity at B-IGH in switched cells even though germline AID hotspot density is not significantly different between the loci → chromatin/architecture/regulatory rather than intrinsic-motif difference; (e) V-gene family usage differs sharply — A-IGH VH1 upregulated in IgG vs IgM, B-IGH VH7 upregulated in IgG vs IgM; (f) positive-selection signature (Σ>0 in CDRs) reaches significance only for A-IGH IgG/IgA rearrangements. Interpretation: A-IGH is the dominant class-switched, high-affinity, mucosal (IgA-heavy) compartment; B-IGH is a more diverse, less affinity-matured, more-IgM-heavy compartment — functional partition of the humoral response across two chromosomes. Implications: bats' role as viral reservoirs may hinge on this dual-response architecture; conventional germline databases, repertoire assemblers, and antibody-annotation tools built on a single-locus mammalian assumption will mis-call bat repertoires; and the finding overturns the general "single IgH locus in mammals" principle. Third, Passon/Bandera/Mayerhöfer/De Smedt/Svilenov (TUM Biopharmaceutical Technology + Ghent Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences; J Pharm Sci doi:10.1016/j.xphs.2026.104447, 2026-07-31 online-ahead-of-print): "Physicochemical developability insights into human Fab fragments with extended hypervariable loops." Abstract-only summary — full text is behind Elsevier auth wall and no preprint located. Panel: 5 human Fabs with long CDR-H3 loops in the heavy chain, tested for secretion, homogeneity (protein-A elution), conformational stability (thermal/chemical denaturation), colloidal stability (self-interaction and diffusion coefficients), and non-specific binding (cross-interaction chromatography + BVP-ELISA), complemented by all-atom MD simulations to interpret loop conformation and residue-level flexibility. Headline finding: the 5 Fabs' liabilities distribute across the developability panel without correlating with CDR-H3 length — sequence composition and MD-observed loop dynamics drive the observed problems (secretion, aggregation, non-specific binding), not length. Argues against blanket length-based early-stage filters on extended-CDR-H3 candidates and for mechanistically-informed sequence-and-dynamics-aware developability triage. Note in the audio: this item is going off the abstract only because the paper is behind a subscription wall.

item.title: AlphaFold3 antibody-antigen benchmark (Zheng lab, UT Health Houston, bioRxiv 2026-07-31) — 3,401 SAbDab complexes + 23,798 negative controls; max recall 53% at 100 seeds, precision 64%, F1 0.53; PAE<2.5 or IPTM>0.7 threshold; 3% false-positive rate hallucinating plausible epitopes across ordered globular surfaces but never onto disordered regions; X-ray-derived antibodies recall 52% vs EM-derived 30% (22-point gap); positive rate drops with target size/surface area; CDR composition, CDR length, and training-set leakage (2,323/3,401 leaked) all statistically null on prediction bias; ~34% of false negatives retain correct epitope location despite poor structural alignment — conformation refinement recovery lever; disorder-truncation and refinement passes as concrete remediation. Tetrahedral antibody architectures (Capon, Hinge Bio, bioRxiv v2 2026-07-31) — non-Y-shaped multispecific IgG scaffold self-assembles via two hinge-integrated collectrin-like domains (CLDs); dual-Fc anti-CD19/CD20 candidate translating clinically for SLE; anti-SARS-CoV-2 ACE2-740 superdimer neutralizes 403-fold better than planar ACE2-615 dimer; ACE2-740/B13A bispecific tetrahedral 646-fold better than ACE2-740 dimer, 29-fold vs parental B13A mAb; ACE2-740/615 tetrahedral IC50=16 pM against Omicron B.1.1.529 (2 orders-of-magnitude gain vs prior mAbs); 8 FDA-approved therapeutic Fabs tested — tetrahedral reformat consistently outperforms parental IgG; Tg32 FcRn transgenic mouse t1/2 10.6-11.2 d (bispecific) and 16.3-17.6 d (pure IgG tetrahedrals) — competitive with 12-15 d parental IgG; functional FcgammaR cooperativity across dual-Fc; CLD-interface disulfide bond resolves quaternary heterogeneity; in vivo NHP prophylactic efficacy for anti-SARS-CoV-2 tetrahedral. PLM twilight-zone embedding benchmark (Bhattacharya, Auburn U at Montgomery, bioRxiv 2026-07-31) — head-to-head evaluation of ESM-1b, ESM-2, ProtT5, ProstT5 for alignment-free structural similarity via mean-pooled embeddings on 20,445 PISCES pairs at ≤30% sequence identity, TM-align TMmin ground truth; ProstT5 + cosine similarity Spearman 0.676 (best), ESM-2 0.623, ProtT5 0.557, ESM-1b 0.483; all four beat BLASTP, with the gain most pronounced at lowest identities; cosine is best metric across all models; dot product and raw Euclidean catastrophic on ESM-2 (0.044 and 0.166) — magnitude-normalization essential; ProstT5's structure-aware pretraining (3Di tokens via AlphaFold-DB) transfers to sequence-only inference and outperforms same-parameter-count pure sequence models at lower embedding dimension (1024 vs ESM-2's 2560) — Pareto improvement for structural downstream tasks.
item.description: Saturday morning edition — three items, all bioRxiv preprints posted 2026-07-31. First, Solanki/Maurya/Ramlakhan/Li/Chen/Wu/Zheng (McWilliams School of Biomedical Informatics, UT Health Science Center at Houston + Weill Cornell; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.07.30.741792v1, bioinformatics, 2026-07-31): "A Structural Antibody Benchmark of AlphaFold3 reveals Hallucinated Epitopes and a Bias for Orderness." Dataset: 3,401 non-redundant antibody-antigen complexes from SAbDab (variable-fragment sequences, union-Chothia/Kabat/IMGT CDR annotation) as positive controls; two kinds of negatives — One-to-One (3,401 antibodies paired with randomly sampled 50-500 residue human proteins verified for low sequence similarity to true antigen) and Many-to-One (each antibody vs six fixed proteins from six organisms: rat parvalbumin PVALB, Drosophila CG6073, E. coli araB, cow CLIC4, Arabidopsis DGR2, human CD274/PD-L1) — 23,798 total negatives. AF3 inference at 10 seeds initially; false negatives re-run at 100 seeds. Binary classifier: PAE<2.5 or IPTM>0.7. Whole-benchmark performance: 46% recall, 64% precision, F1 0.53, 90% accuracy (inflated by ~20K true negatives, flagged in the paper). 100-seed rerun pushes recall ceiling to 53%. Four findings. X-ray vs electron-microscopy split: 2,059 X-ray-derived antibodies recall 52% vs 1,342 EM-derived antibodies at 30% — 22-point gap. Two proposed drivers: (1) X-ray PDBs overrepresented in AF3 training set (batch effect learned by the model even though leakage per se was statistically null — see below); (2) X-ray-tractable proteins are systematically less flexible and less disordered than EM-solved targets, since cryo-EM captures the hard-to-crystallize flexible cases. Disorderness/target size: positive prediction rate drops monotonically with target protein length and convex-hull volume/surface area on the Many-to-One batches. Mechanism demonstrated on batch F (CD274/PD-L1, 290 residues, 27% disordered, prominent N-terminal disordered alpha-helix): when they superimpose all false-positive antibodies predicted against PD-L1, none of the hallucinated interfaces land on the disordered region — AF3 hallucinates plausible epitopes across the ordered globular surface but not onto disordered regions. Practical implication: truncate disordered regions before running AF3 to reduce search-space cost, since disorder was already protected from hallucination. Factors that didn't matter: (a) Data leakage — 2,323 of 3,401 positive-control antibodies had leaked into AF3 training (intersection of 195,858 training CIF files with SAbDab-sourced PDBs); PAE distributions on leaked vs unseen antibodies were statistically indistinguishable within each batch, so AF3 is not merely memorizing training structures. (b) CDR amino-acid composition — residue-frequency histograms of positive vs negative predictions are indistinguishable across all 6 CDRs; even the frequency ordering matches. (c) CDR length — no correlation with prediction success. (d) Antibody "stickiness" — Pearson correlation of 0.997 between false-positive rates of antibodies predicted correctly against their true antigen vs antibodies predicted as false negatives, meaning AF3 hallucinates specific complementary epitopes per antibody rather than treating some antibodies as generically sticky. False-negative recovery potential: DockQ + epitope-shift + antibody-displacement scoring shows ~34% of the ~1,500 false negatives from the 10-seed run retain correct epitope location despite poor structural alignment quality — one-third of the missed antibodies are close enough that conformation refinement (molecular dynamics, increased AF3 recycling parameter, interface-focused sampling) could rescue them without needing more data. Discussion recommends this as the main follow-on investment. Overall AF3 antibody-antigen headline number: 53% recall, 3% false-positive rate, on a large non-redundant benchmark with proper negative controls. Second, Capon/Troitskaya/Fomin/Gefter/Chan (Hinge Bio, Redwood City + Vitalant Research Institute + German Primate Center + Charité Berlin + Universität Göttingen; bioRxiv doi:10.1101/2022.03.23.485397v2, molecular biology, 2026-07-31): "Topologically Engineered Tetrahedral Antibody Architectures for Multispecific Therapy." Architecture: co-express a collectrin-like domain (CLD, the dimerization module of ACE2 and SGLT1 accessory) as a hinge insertion in the IgG heavy chain. Two heavy chains pair via CLDs, and two such pairs cross-dimerize via a second reciprocal CLD interface, yielding a "superdimer" — a rigid tetrahedral-like quaternary architecture projecting two Fc dimers and two additional effector-domain dimers outward from a central CLD nucleus. Six unobstructed binding arms possible (4 Fabs + 2 Fcs; 4 ECDs + 2 Fcs; mixed). Structural homogeneity: initial constructs yield superdimer/dimer mixtures; restricting to a single pair of CLD-dimerizing polypeptides guides assembly into a defined tetrahedral form. Anti-SARS-CoV-2 demonstrations: ACE2-740 superdimer neutralizes SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus 403-fold better than planar ACE2-615 dimer, HCoV-NL63 87-fold; bispecific ACE2-740/B13A tetrahedral 646-fold better than ACE2-740 dimer and 29-fold vs parental B13A mAb; ACE2-740/615 tetrahedral (designated HB1507) IC50 16 pM against Omicron B.1.1.529 — two orders of magnitude improvement over historical authorized mAbs. Generality of platform: tetravalent monospecific Fab-Fab tetrahedrals built from Fabs of 8 FDA-approved/authorized therapeutic antibodies (REGN10933, VIR7831, etc.) — all outperform parental bivalent IgG on pseudovirus neutralization. Pharmacokinetics: Tg32 human FcRn transgenic mice, single 10 mg/kg i.v. bolus; ACE2-740/B13A-WT and ACE2-740/B13A-HA (catalytically inactive) terminal t1/2 = 10.6 and 11.2 days (33.5- and 35.4-fold extension over soluble ACE2 APN01's 7.6-h clinical t1/2); pure IgG tetrahedrals REGN10933-REGN10933 and VIR7831-VIR7831 t1/2 = 17.6 and 16.3 days — competitive with parental IgG t1/2 of 12.9 and 14.7 days. CLD nucleus does not compromise FcRn-mediated recycling. Fc-gamma receptor cooperativity: functional binding across dual-Fc domains of anti-CD19/CD20 tetrahedral antibody demonstrated. Structural stability: introducing an interface disulfide bond into the CLD dimer effectively abolishes dynamic dissociation and resolves the quaternary equilibrium into discrete stable states — solving the assembly-heterogeneity problem. Clinical translation: anti-CD19/CD20 tetrahedral heading to clinic for systemic lupus erythematosus; anti-SARS-CoV-2 tetrahedrals show in vivo prophylactic efficacy in non-human primates. Broad neutralization across 12 SARS-CoV-2 variants including Omicron. Design implication for structure-predictor and generative-design tools: tetrahedral topology and CLD-mediated non-covalent self-assembly add a design axis outside the standard IgG-centric multispecific formats, and the CLD dimerization interface is a well-defined structural constraint that could go directly into Boltz/Chai templates. Third, Danwada/Udomprasert/Raychawdhary/Seals/Wu/Bhattacharya (Auburn University at Montgomery + Auburn University main campus; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.07.31.742099v1, bioinformatics, 2026-07-31): "Evaluating Protein Language Model Embeddings for Structural Similarity in the Protein-Sequence Twilight Zone." Question: on protein pairs at ≤30% sequence identity where BLAST fails, how well do mean-pooled PLM embeddings predict structural similarity? Benchmark: 20,445 PISCES pairs ≤30% identity, TM-align TMmin as structural ground truth. Four PLMs: ESM-1b (650M params, 1280-dim, encoder-only), ESM-2 (3B params, 2560-dim, encoder-only), ProtT5 (3B params, 1024-dim, T5 encoder-decoder), ProstT5 (same T5 backbone as ProtT5 but pretrained with AlphaFold-DB-derived 3Di structural tokens as auxiliary objective; sequence-only at inference with an <AA2fold> control token, 1024-dim). Five similarity metrics on mean-pooled embeddings: cosine, Euclidean-derived, RBF kernel, Manhattan-derived, dot product. Headline Spearman correlations with TMmin, best metric per model in bold in the paper: ProstT5 cosine 0.676; ESM-2 cosine 0.623 (Euclidean 0.166, dot product 0.044 — magnitude-normalization essential for ESM-2); ProtT5 cosine 0.557; ESM-1b cosine 0.483. All four PLMs beat BLASTP, with the advantage most pronounced at the lowest sequence identities — exactly the regime where classical alignment breaks down. ProstT5 lead over pure sequence models even though inference sees no structural input: training-time 3Di signal transfers into a genuinely structure-aware sequence embedding. Efficiency: ProstT5's 1024-dim residue-level embedding is cheaper to store and to compare pairwise than ESM-2's 2560-dim embedding, so on residue-level embedding cost ProstT5 is a Pareto improvement for structural downstream tasks. Practical recommendations for antibody-ML groups: for structural downstream tasks (remote homology, epitope-similarity clustering, fold classification), prefer ProstT5 over ESM-2 as the frozen backbone; use cosine similarity by default and avoid dot product / raw Euclidean on ESM-2 specifically. For sequence-level generation or masked infilling, the trade-off is different and outside this paper's scope.

item.title: APB-Display v2 (Fordyce lab, Stanford, bioRxiv 2026-07-17) — in vitro hydrogel-bead platform for absolute Kd at scale via emulsion PCR + IVTT + SNAP-tag (~800,000 copies/bead); APB-TiteSeq: 7-concentration FACS + deep sequencing returns thermodynamic Kd values, R²=0.96 vs fluorescence polarization, <1.4-fold resolution (0.3 kT), 18,000+ FLAG variants in 3 days at $0.15/variant; chemistry-dependent epistasis between FLAG positions 4 and 5 identified in 23,000-member library; APB-SortSeq: single-concentration + neural-network denoising extends to 88,000+ variants; overcomes yeast/phage display enrichment-score limitations by returning absolute Kd for direct thermodynamic regression. SemVac (bioRxiv 2026-07-17) — 14 LLMs benchmarked for zero-shot protective-antigen discovery from biomedical literature text; text reasoning matches specialized deep-learning classifiers (VaxiJen, NERVE) in precision without fine-tuning on labeled antigens; chain-of-thought increases recall but consistently reduces precision (over-reasoning pitfall); Mpox proteome sweep recapitulates known protective antigens + identifies B20R as novel candidate via semantic immune-evasion + surface-exposure signal. EnzGFM (Shen lab, Johns Hopkins + Shanghai AI Lab, Nat Commun 2026-07-17) — Mamba-Transformer hybrid enzyme-specific protein language model with hierarchical pre-training; 2-5x faster than Transformer baselines; +16.67% kinetic parameter prediction, +15.69% enzyme-reaction mapping, +13.19% EC classification, +20.04% mutation effect assessment; EnzGFM-Agent agentic pipeline for enzyme engineering candidate selection
item.description: Saturday morning edition — three items. First, Fordyce lab (Stanford; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.05.28.728566, v2 posted 2026-07-17, biophysics): Amplicon/Protein Bead Display (APB-Display) — a fully in vitro, bead-based platform returning absolute Kd values across protein variant libraries at scale. Core motivation: cell-based display assays return enrichment scores confounded by folding efficiency, surface trafficking, and post-translational modifications, not thermodynamic Kd; APB-Display eliminates all three confounds. Architecture: hydrogel beads dual-functionalized with oligonucleotides (DNA capture) and benzylguanine groups (covalent protein attachment via SNAP tag). Workflow step 1: emulsion PCR using particle-templated emulsification (foam tube + vortex mixer, no microfluidics) under Poisson conditions → clonal Amplicon Beads each bearing one variant's sequence at high copy number. Workflow step 2: second emulsification with IVTT reagents → variant protein expressed and attached via N-terminal SNAP tag at ~800,000 copies per bead alongside the template DNA amplicon. Full workflow library-DNA to protein-decorated beads: <8 hours with standard lab equipment. Affinity measurement (APB-TiteSeq): incubate bead library with fluorescently-labeled antibody at 7 concentrations (0.6-400 nM shown for M2 anti-FLAG/FLAG octapeptide system); multi-bin FACS sorting at each concentration + deep sequencing of variant identities within each bin; Kd extracted by fitting Langmuir isotherm to per-variant concentration-response curves. FLAG epitope single-substitution landscape (153 variants): <3 days, $0.15/variant, thermodynamic resolution <1.4-fold (<0.3 kcal/mol = 0.3 kT); validation vs fluorescence polarization on 7 variants: R²=0.96. APB-TiteSeq scale-up: 23,283-variant library (pairwise + quadruple combinations at 4 FLAG positions); completed in 3 days, Kd values returned for >18,000 variants. Within this landscape: chemistry-dependent epistasis between FLAG positions 4 and 5 — the energetic contribution of a substitution at position 4 depends on the residue at position 5, a coupling invisible in single-substitution scans. APB-SortSeq: single-concentration sort + neural-network denoising step recovers quantitative affinities from noisier single-point data; demonstrated on 88,000+ variant library. Implications for antibody ML: FLAG/M2 is an established antibody-epitope model system with a published co-crystal structure; the dataset provides ground-truth Kd for CDR sequence-to-affinity regressor training/benchmarking; the in vitro format removes cell-surface artifacts; absolute Kd values slot directly into thermodynamic regression models; the platform is sequence-agnostic and could be applied to CDR loops on fixed frameworks; the neural-network denoising in APB-SortSeq is an inference-time uncertainty-reduction method worth noting for high-throughput assay design in general. Second, Zhao/Shu et al. (Chinese institutions; bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.07.13.737696, v1 posted 2026-07-17, immunology): SemVac — Semantic Vaccinology, a framework for zero-shot protective antigen discovery using large language model text reasoning. Motivation: classical reverse vaccinology (sequence-based classifiers — VaxiJen, NERVE) trained on small validated-antigen sets struggle with functionally ambiguous proteins where no clear sequence signature of protective potential exists; LLMs may leverage compressed biomedical literature knowledge to recover a complementary antigen signal. Method: zero-shot text reasoning — given a protein name, query the LLM about its protective antigen potential; no antigen-specific fine-tuning. Benchmark: 14 current-generation LLMs tested on a curated dataset of validated and non-validated antigens. Primary finding: text-reasoning LLMs match or exceed specialized deep-learning models (VaxiJen, NERVE) in precision — knowledge compressed into pretrained representations from scientific literature is sufficient to recover a meaningful antigen prediction signal without task-specific training. Secondary finding (over-reasoning pitfall): chain-of-thought prompting consistently increases recall (more true antigens identified) but consistently reduces precision (LLMs generate plausible-sounding but incorrect reasoning chains leading to false-positive antigen predictions); chain-of-thought expands the antigen-candidate funnel at the cost of increased false-positive experimental burden. Application to complete Mpox proteome: SemVac recapitulates all established protective antigens and flags B20R as a previously unrecognized candidate; semantic analysis links B20R to immune evasion mechanisms and surface structural exposure — the biological signatures expected of a protective antigen; experimental validation remains required. Utility for antibody campaigns: antigen selection is the upstream bottleneck; LLM text reasoning as a proteome-scale literature sweep is a useful complement to sequence classifiers, especially for pathogens with limited experimental antigen data; the recall-precision tradeoff of chain-of-thought has direct implications for how to design downstream experimental adjudication. Third, Shen/Wu et al. (Shen lab, Johns Hopkins + Henan Medical University + Shanghai AI Lab; Nature Communications doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75283-3, published 2026-07-17): EnzGFM — enzyme-specific protein language model with Mamba-Transformer hybrid architecture and hierarchical pre-training. Architecture: Mamba (state-space model, linear-time sequence processing vs quadratic Transformer attention) layered with Transformer encoder for combined long-range + local pattern capture; hierarchical pre-training at multiple sequence levels. Benchmark performance (relative improvements over Transformer-based baselines at comparable parameter counts): kinetic parameter prediction +16.67%; enzyme-reaction mapping +15.69%; EC number classification +13.19%; mutation effect assessment +20.04%; inference speed 2-5× faster than Transformer baselines. Extension: EnzGFM-Agent — agentic pipeline for automated enzyme engineering candidate selection, with claimed experimental enrichment of beneficial variants. Architectural relevance beyond enzymes: Mamba-Transformer hybrids address the quadratic attention bottleneck that limits Transformer PLMs on long sequences; antibody PLMs may benefit for paired heavy-light chain co-modeling where long-range intra- and inter-chain dependencies matter; the antibody language model field remains largely Transformer-based — EnzGFM is a working example that the architecture space is open.
